clusters.title: The ROCm fused QK-norm kernel rejects fp32 norm weights

cause_prs.author: ZhengGong-amd
cause_prs.title: [Perf] [AMD] qknorm: Use the fused in-place QK norm kernel on ROCm

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
First seen in the Scout run at 20:09 UTC Nov 21. The test fails in all three ROCm versions.

It passed in [PR Test, Nov 21 13:08, rocm10](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/44907362892), whose code ([`b959096e`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/b959096ecfac779048a1926eeda2f6cd173becf3)) predates the PR.
No scheduled PR Test has run on code that includes the PR yet.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#39071](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39071) ([`77c393a7`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/77c393a7beae720dfc3a6b4cf44f7aedbfedabc0)), merged 13:50 UTC, turned on the fused in-place QK-norm JIT path for HIP in `apply_qk_norm`.
The gate checks only `q.dtype`. A bf16 q with fp32 norm weights now reaches `qknorm.cuh:197`, which accepts only bf16 weights.
The traceback runs through the changed branch.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the Scout run uses an aiter override ([`09497204`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/09497204a230a265b419f27965563ed5325c9562)), so there is no A/B with the default aiter yet. The check that fails is sglang's own kernel code, not aiter.
Side effect `[LOW]`: ROCm models that keep fp32 QK-norm weights with bf16 activations could hit the same error. No serving test has shown this yet.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: run `test_qk_norm_rope_hip.py -k fp32_norm_weight` at `77c393a7` and at `77c393a7^` with the default aiter, and watch the Nov 22 01:10 PR Test.

rows: `Dtype value [float32] not in the allowed options: [bfloat16]`

clusters.title: Out-of-tree platform unit tests fail because an earlier test leaves `current_platform` set

cause_prs.author: De-cs
cause_prs.title: [Feat] [NPU] diffusion: Integrate MindIE-SD quantized attention into Ascend FA

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
Failed in all 3 PR Tests on Nov 21: rocm10 ×2 and rocm724 ×1, always in partition 2.
The file passed in partition 1 on Nov 20 13:10.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#46029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46029) ([`ba9c86bb`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/ba9c86bb7eee016a3d5943f4dfe3d8daf0ad7e0a)) added `monkeypatch.setattr(platforms, "current_platform", …)` at `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py:702`.
When pytest 9.0.3 undoes the patch, it writes the real ROCm platform back as a plain module attribute. Later `patch.object(platforms, "_current_platform", …)` calls then have no effect.
New unit files moved both files into the same partition on Nov 21. The failure follows that partition: 3 of 3 jobs where the files share a partition failed, and 0 of 8 where they don't.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: not reproduced with the real files on a ROCm machine, only with a small pytest example. The PR merged Nov 17, before the last passing run, so it is not inside a pass→fail window.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found. The related [#51734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51734) (open since Nov 20) does not cover line 702.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: run `pytest …/test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py::test_npu_falls_back_from_pipelined_attention …/test_oot_platform_runtime.py -p no:randomly` in the CI image, then run the OOT file alone.

clusters.title: MI355X disagg: every 4-node Slurm allocation stays pending until the 180-min step timeout

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:

4 of the 4 finished `nightly-mi355x-4n` configs in the [Nov 21 04:08 run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/44864621205) timed out with `JobState=PENDING Reason=Resources`. The first was submitted at 10:47 UTC, and the last was still pending at 20:02.
7 more 4-node configs are queued.
All finished 2-node configs passed. The 4-node configs last passed on Nov 19.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` infrastructure; no change is blamed.
At least one of the 4 `amd-sglang` nodes was down, drained or held by another job. `pit2-p03-g26` is missing from every allocation today and was used on Nov 19.
The launcher counts `PENDING` as alive (`launch_mi355x.sh:1832-1840`), so each config spends its full 3 h before failing.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the logs have no `sinfo` output, so the node's state is inferred from its absence. It is related to, but not the same as, yesterday's `QOSGrpNodeLimit` wait.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found. [#49956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49956) only cleans up stale allocations. [#51399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51399) would add more load on the same 4 nodes.
Cluster owners: run `sinfo -p amd-sglang -R`, `scontrol show node pit2-p03-g26`, and `sacct -j 29856,29868,29878,29918`.
Consider adding a deadline for allocations that never start.
